bib.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs? A Comprehensive Study and Hybrid Approach

question: How do RAG and long-context LLMs compare on performance and cost, and can the two be combined?
hypothesis: RAG acts as a prior that focuses attention, while large-scale pretraining may give LC stronger ability; a hybrid routing queries by self-reflection can keep LC accuracy at RAG cost.
contributions: Systematic benchmark of RAG vs LC with three LLMs on nine real datasets
SELF-ROUTE, routing queries to RAG or LC by model self-reflection
Analysis: RAG failure reasons, k ablation, retrievers, synthetic data, parametric knowledge

method.summary: Compare RAG (top-k 300-word chunks) against feeding the full context to three LLMs on nine long-context QA datasets. SELF-ROUTE first runs RAG with an option to answer 'unanswerable'; unanswerable queries get the full context.

limits: Cost is proxied by input tokens; retrieval cost excluded (footnote 1 says retrieval is easy to host).
Black-box LLMs with possible data leakage of Wikipedia-based datasets; authors call it an open question.
Synthetic benchmarks (PassKey) are shown to be artifact-prone, so RAG vs LC conclusions there are unreliable.
Single run, no decoding settings, temperature, or variance reported.
Self-Route assumes LLMs are well calibrated at saying unanswerable; OpenAI models reject more often than Gemini so the trade-off differs.
Optimal k depends on task; k=5 lowest cost on average but k=1 on NarrativeQA and QMSum.
Internal inconsistencies between text and tables (answerable %, GPT-4O averages, LC gap percentages).
Only three 2024 models; results may have dated.
